newsitem.title: USA: GLICKMAN OPTIMISTIC ON EGYPT BIOTECH GRAIN DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: GLICKMAN OPTIMISTIC ON EGYPT BIOTECH GRAIN DISPUTE.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday he expects the Egyptian government to act soon to resolve a dispute with the United States about imports of genetically altered crops.

Glickman met with the Egyptian ambassador in Washington on August 7 to express U.S. concerns about an order issued by Egypt's Health Ministry, effective July 1, that requires proof that grain imported for human consumption has not been genetically altered.
"I'm optimistic that we'll get it resolved. The meeting was quite cordial," Glickman told Reuters after a speech at the Illinois State Fair.

Glickman said Egypt was a major buyer of U.S. grains and keeping the country as a customer was a priority. But the United States has repeatedly said genetically altered crops have been proven safe and should require no labeling or segregation.

Last month Glickman told a meeting of agribusiness lobbyists in Washington that food safety issues tied to genetically altered crops would be the subject of debate between food producers and consumers for years to come.
"This is really shaping up to be the battle royal of 21st century agriculture," Glickman said. ((Emily Kaiser, 312 408 8720))
